headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and network data while LightZero is local-only, creating unsafe pairings by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly inject instructions into nullclaw. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of outputs into nullclaw's stdin/stdout, files, or web channels, which is an unusual configuration. nullclaw's permissive input surfaces make it the more exposed side, but the pairwise pathway is not default.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are manually pasted into nullclaw prompts or web channels, injection becomes possible.
IF nullclaw ingests file or stdin content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep LightZero and nullclaw on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into nullclaw unless reviewed.
Use a fixed prompt wrapper that labels imported text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before nullclaw tool use.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, but nullclaw reads and writes workspace files, audit logs, and secrets such as API keys and bearer tokens. If the pair shares a workspace or operator-visible files, nullclaw can expose sensitive material while LightZero remains local-only. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents share ~/.nullclaw/workspace or another common directory, nullclaw can read sensitive files accessible there.
IF operator places secrets in files that nullclaw indexes or logs, those secrets may appear in outputs or audit logs.
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Restrict nullclaw workspace permissions to non-sensitive files.
Review audit logs before sharing them externally.
requires-engineering: separate secret-bearing and non-secret workspaces.
requires-engineering: add redaction before any network egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files or modify git, so it does not contend for mutable resources. nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, creating overlap only if the operator gives both agents the same writable directory or repo. Because one side lacks write capability, this is not high, but the conflict pathway exists in common setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable repository, nullclaw can overwrite artifacts LightZero expects to remain stable.
IF the operator enables shared git or filesystem access, concurrent edits can race without locking.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid sharing a git checkout between the agents.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in its own container volume.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero can generate game-playing outputs, and nullclaw can consume external inputs and act through tools, webhooks, or scheduling. If nullclaw treats LightZero's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks built-in verification evidence, so the pathway is inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are forwarded into nullclaw without a verification step, nullclaw may act on incorrect recommendations.
IF nullclaw is configured to send emails, webhooks, or other actions based on imported text, cascading errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any action-taking step.
Add a verification prompt that checks LightZero outputs against source data.
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for imported content.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before tool execution.
requires-engineering: add structured validation for all LightZero-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for LightZero, while nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, conversation history, workspace files, and audit logs. Because the pair lacks evidence of PHI, EU PII, or a cross-border policy conflict, compliance risk is limited to documented gaps around secret handling and logging rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into nullclaw's workspace or logs, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF the operator routes PHI or EU PII through nullclaw without a DPA or HIPAA controls, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in shared workspaces.
Review retention settings before enabling logging.
Use a data-classification checklist before each run.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data.
